resource.valueString: Alert and oriented; courteous, dryly funny even while tearful; speech normal; mood "hollow"; talks of his wife in the present tense and keeps her room as it was; yearning and preoccupation every day; some days wishes he could join her, without any intent or plan; no hallucinations apart from sometimes hearing her voice as he falls asleep, which he knows is not real; thinking clear

Current ideation present; intent absent; plan absent; access reviewed true. Disposition: Outpatient care with weekly visits and a telephone call in three days. Passive thoughts of death (wishing he could join his wife) without intent, plan or preparation; no past suicide attempt. Older widowed men are at high risk of suicide in the years after a loss (a Danish register study found the highest rise in suicide risk in the oldest bereaved men), and he has several further risk factors: repeated bereavement, living through the anniversary of her death, insomnia, alcohol each evening, chronic illness and social withdrawal. Means safety: no firearms in the house; medicines kept in small supplies; he agreed to keep whisky to one glass and none on bad nights. A written safety plan was made with him, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit.

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Geriatric psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis, separate prolonged grief disorder from major depression, advise on grief therapy, medicine and sleep, and review suicide risk
  • Safety: a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in his phone, means safety, a telephone call in three days, and safety review at every visit
  • Prolonged grief disorder therapy (Shear): sixteen weekly sessions with a trained psychologist, covering the story of the death, imaginal conversations with his wife, memories and pictures, revisiting avoided places and things, and personal goals; PG-13-R and PHQ-9 every four weeks; no antidepressant unless major depression develops
  • Sleep: a fixed rising time, no naps after noon, no cigar or whisky in the last hours before bed, and getting up if awake more than twenty minutes; no benzodiazepine, zolpidem or sedating antihistamine
  • Tobacco: his readiness asked at every visit; brief advice linked to his own concern about his heart; counseling at each visit and the state quitline; varenicline offered as the most effective single medicine, with combination nicotine replacement as the alternative
  • Chest tightness on exertion: resting ECG today and CT coronary angiography, chosen over stress testing for a man over 65 with stable symptoms and no known coronary disease; call 911 for chest pain at rest or lasting more than fifteen minutes
  • Nonobstructive coronary disease: atorvastatin 40 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks later and a goal of at least a 50 percent fall in LDL, aspirin 81 mg, blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg, stopping smoking, and walking most days
  • Gout: allopurinol from 100 mg daily, raised by 100 mg every two to five weeks to a serum urate below 6 mg/dL, with colchicine 0.6 mg daily for three to six months to prevent flares; flares treated without stopping allopurinol; HLA-B*58:01 testing not indicated by ancestry; less alcohol
  • Social connection and his writing: one planned social contact a week, a return to morning writing on a set project, and the clinic social worker's list of local groups; meaning and goals to be part of any grief treatment
  • Gout: urate measured at intake; urate-lowering therapy explained, since two flares in a year make it strongly recommended; he chose to decide after the chest evaluation; call at the first sign of a flare
  • Cardiovascular risk: blood pressure at each visit and lipids, hemoglobin A1c and kidney function at baseline; prediabetes (hemoglobin A1c 5.8 percent) managed with walking and diet

resource.title: Mark Twain synthetic care plan
resource.description: Prolonged grief disorder in a 69-year-old writer and humorist a year after his wife's death, after the earlier deaths of a son and a daughter. The episode covers the DSM-5-TR criteria and the PG-13-R; telling prolonged grief from normal grief and from major depression with the PHQ-9 and a clinical interview, and the decision not to start an antidepressant when major depression is absent; a structured safety assessment for passive thoughts of death in an older bereaved man, who is at high risk of suicide, with means safety and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; prolonged grief disorder therapy (Shear) in sixteen weekly sessions; sleep without sedative-hypnotics; tobacco use disorder in a cigar smoker since boyhood, with counseling and varenicline under the USPSTF recommendation; exertional chest tightness evaluated with an ECG and CT coronary angiography under the 1900 chest pain guideline, and nonobstructive coronary disease treated with a high-intensity statin and aspirin; gout with allopurinol started low and raised to a urate below 6 mg/dL, with colchicine prophylaxis and a flare treated without stopping allopurinol, under the ACR 1899 guideline; and social connection and his writing as part of recovery.
